memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now the earth was corrupt in God's sight and was full of violence. God saw how corrupt the earth had become, for all the people on earth had corrupted their ways. - Gen 6:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Scripture now shows us why judgement was necessary. Twice it repeats the word "corrupt," and it adds that the earth was "full of violence." The inward corruption of the heart (v.5) had spilled out into outward violence - cruelty, oppression, and bloodshed everywhere. What began in sinful hearts had poisoned an entire society.

This is the tragic logic of sin. It never stays private. A corrupt heart produces corrupt actions, and enough corrupt people produce a corrupt world. Violence - the strong crushing the weak, people harming one another - is what happens when human beings live as though God does not see and will not judge.

It is worth noticing that God "saw." Nothing escapes His notice. He sees the violence and injustice of every age, including our own. To the victims of a violent world, this is deep comfort: God sees, and He cares, and He will one day set all things right.

We are not so different from Noah's world. Our world too is often full of violence and corruption. But we are called to be people of a different spirit - peacemakers, not oppressors. "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God" (Matt 5:9). And we look forward to the day when Christ returns to establish a kingdom of perfect justice and peace, where violence is no more (Isa 2:4).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God sees the injustice and violence of our world?
- Are you a peacemaker in your corner of a broken world?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Righteous God, You see the violence and corruption of our world, and You care. Make me a peacemaker, and hasten the day when Christ makes all things right.
